skill.name: github-project-management
skill.description: Manage GitHub issues, project boards, sprint planning, and swarm-coordinated project workflows.
skill.summary: Guides AI-assisted GitHub project management across issues, boards, sprints, and progress reporting.
skill.author: Claude Code

security_audit.summary: Static findings are mostly Markdown code fences, inline code, placeholder URLs, and CLI examples; no prompt-injection text or hidden malicious instructions were found. The main risks are operational: unpinned npx tools and examples that can mutate GitHub issues or projects if run without review.

remediation.issue: External tools are invoked through npx without stable version guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Pin ruv-swarm and claude-flow versions, document trusted installation steps, and ask users to confirm package provenance before execution.

remediation.issue: Some examples close issues, change labels, or sync across organizations.
remediation.suggestion: Add dry-run commands and explicit confirmation steps before destructive or cross-organization GitHub operations.

remediation.issue: Webhook and reporting examples can disclose project metadata if configured incorrectly.
remediation.suggestion: Document webhook authentication, private repository data handling, and allowed destinations for board updates.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned External Tool Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs users to run npx claude-flow@alpha and many unpinned npx ruv-swarm commands. These commands can execute npm-distributed code while GitHub CLI credentials are available.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Multiple examples directly invoke npx packages. The package names match the skill purpose, but unpinned remote execution creates supply-chain risk in an authenticated GitHub workflow.

semantic_findings.title: Automated GitHub Mutation Requires Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The skill includes examples that close duplicate or stale issues and synchronize data across organizations. Running these workflows without confirmation can change repository state or propagate incorrect data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples explicitly close issues, modify labels, and sync across organizations. These are legitimate project-management actions, but they need explicit user approval and rollback planning.

content.user_title: Manage GitHub Projects With Swarm Workflows
content.value_statement: GitHub project work can become hard to track across issues, boards, and sprints. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured workflows for coordinated issue and project management.
actual_capabilities: Creates and triages GitHub issues with labels, assignees, and structured templates.
Converts issues into swarm tasks, subtasks, and progress checklists.
Defines project board setup, status mapping, synchronization, and dashboard workflows.
Supports sprint planning, milestone tracking, board analytics, and progress reports.
Provides templates for integration tasks, bugs, feature requests, and swarm tasks.
Includes troubleshooting and security guidance for permissions, audit logs, and webhooks.
limitations: Requires GitHub CLI authentication and repository permissions before commands can work.
Depends on ruv-swarm, claude-flow, or matching MCP tools being installed and trusted.
Many examples can modify live GitHub issues, labels, projects, or comments.
Provides workflow guidance and command examples, not a standalone application.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Feature Delivery
use_cases.description: Break a feature request into issues, subtasks, board cards, and progress updates.

use_cases.title: Improve Issue Triage
use_cases.description: Analyze unlabeled issues, suggest labels, detect duplicates, and prepare review queues.

use_cases.title: Track Sprint Health
use_cases.description: Create sprint plans, monitor milestones, and generate board metrics for team review.

prompt_templates.title: Triage New Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the open GitHub issues in this repository. Suggest labels, priorities, possible duplicates, and next actions before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Project Board Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a GitHub project board for this repository. Include columns, fields, labels, sync rules, and a safe rollout plan.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Sprint
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a two-week sprint plan from the current high-priority issues. Include scope, owners, dependencies, risks, and progress reporting.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Cross-Repository Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a cross-repository GitHub workflow for related issues. Include dependency order, board synchronization, conflict handling, and approval checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Plan a sprint for high-priority authentication issues.
output: Sprint goal with selected authentication issues and expected outcomes.
Issue breakdown with owners, dependencies, labels, and board columns.
Progress reporting schedule with review and risk checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Triage unlabeled issues for a repository.
output: Suggested labels and priorities for each issue.
Possible duplicate links and recommended merge or close decisions.
A review queue for issues needing maintainer approval.

output_examples.input: Set up project board automation for a release.
output: Board field plan with status, priority, milestone, and owner fields.
Sync workflow for issues, cards, and release milestones.
Safety checks for permissions, webhooks, and dry-run validation.

best_practices: Review proposed GitHub changes before running commands that modify issues, labels, or projects.
Use least-privilege GitHub tokens and keep audit logs for automated workflows.
Run dry checks before closing issues, syncing boards, or posting automated comments.
anti_patterns: Do not run unpinned npx tools in sensitive repositories without verifying the package source.
Do not let public issue comments trigger privileged automation without authorization checks.
Do not sync private project data to external webhooks without approval and authentication.

faq.question: Does this skill require GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. Many workflows use gh commands and need an authenticated GitHub CLI session.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it create issues automatically?
faq.answer: It provides commands and workflows for issue creation. Users should approve live changes before execution.

faq.question: Can it manage GitHub project boards?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes board setup, synchronization, field mapping, dashboard, and analytics workflows.

faq.question: What permissions are needed?
faq.answer: It needs repository and project permissions that match the requested issue, board, and automation actions.

faq.question: What is the main safety concern?
faq.answer: The main concern is running external tools or mutating GitHub state without review and confirmation.
